sections.h2: Selling an Owatonna house without a long wait
sections.html:
Cash from a buyer who accepts the property exactly as you leave it is usually the quickest way out. A listing with an agent or a sale you arrange yourself takes longer, since both rely on open houses and on a lender approving the buyer.

As the Steele County seat, Owatonna has the recorder, the treasurer and the county finance office all in town. A closing stays simple provided the house has no rental license problems, no delinquent taxes and a clear answer about flooding.

Owners occupy three of every four Owatonna homes. The city sits on both sides of the Straight River, with the oldest neighborhoods on low ground along its eastern side and newer homes along the Maple Creek ravine. Seven public school buildings were repaired or replaced under bonds voters approved in 2015 and 2019, and the new Owatonna High School opened to students on September 5, 2023.

There are 11,018 households here, averaging 2.36 people, and 88.3 percent of residents stayed in the same house for a year.

Record rain from September 22 to 24, 2010 sent the Straight River and Maple Creek over their banks, and developments built in the floodplains of both streams were completely inundated. If you are unsure whether your parcel is in a floodplain, ask the county or city.

If your property sits near the river or the creek, write down any water in the basement, drainage fixes or insurance claims you know about before you list. State law requires a seller to give the buyer written disclosure of known material facts, and past flooding is exactly the sort of fact buyers look for. Keep receipts for sump pumps, regrading or waterproofing, because they help show that a problem was handled.

Every rental in the city must be registered with the Fire Department and hold a city license under Chapter 115 of the city code. An inspection is scheduled, and the license is issued once the property passes and the fees are paid. A license is valid for two years.

  • Use one application per rental address.
  • A new application is needed when a property is rented for the first time, when a license expires, or after a change of ownership.
  • Renting without a valid license is a misdemeanor, and every day of renting counts as a separate violation.

If your Owatonna house is rented, make sure the license is current before the closing date. A buyer planning to keep tenants has to apply for a license after the sale. The Fire Department's number is 507-444-2454.

sections.h2: Steele County Recorder fees and the deed tax
sections.html:
The Steele County Recorder charges $46 to record a document and $54 for a well disclosure statement. Mailed or dropped-off documents are turned around in 10 business days or less, and appointments are available during business hours. A split of a tax parcel carries a $100 fee payable to the county treasurer.

The state deed tax is set by Minnesota Statutes section 287.21. It is 0.33 percent of the net consideration when that exceeds $3,000, and the county collects it when the deed arrives for recording. When there is no consideration, or $3,000 or less, the tax is a flat $1.65.

Before closing, request an itemized settlement statement from the title company that shows the fee, the tax and any unpaid property tax.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and payment options
sections.html:
Steele County mails real estate tax statements each March, and every owner receives one even if a lender pays the bill. Real estate taxes are due in two halves, May 15 and October 15, and a weekend due date rolls to the next business day. Agricultural second-half taxes come due in mid-November, and taxes left unpaid at year end become delinquent on January 1.

Owners can pay in person at the Finance office in the County Administration Building, 630 Florence Avenue, mail a check to Steele County Finance, P.O. Box 890, or use the drop box out front. The drop box is cleared at 8 a.m. the next business day, and later deposits must include a penalty.

  • Cards add 2.5 percent, with a $1.50 minimum.
  • A Visa debit card adds $3.95.
  • E-checks under $10,000 add $1.50.
  • Direct debit carries no fee.

Authorization forms for direct debit must reach the Finance office by April 30 for the first half and September 30 for the second.

sections.h2: A step-by-step plan for a fast Owatonna closing
sections.html: Start about a week before you accept an offer. Check the status of your property tax, since an unpaid balance comes out of your proceeds. If the house is rented, confirm the license with the Fire Department. Write down anything you know about water in the basement, and gather the receipts for pumps or drainage work. When an offer arrives, ask for the closing date, the check amount and who pays each fee in writing. The title company then prepares the deed and the settlement statement. The Recorder charges $46 to record the deed and $54 for the well disclosure, and the county collects the deed tax at recording. Review the itemized settlement statement before you sign, so the numbers match the offer.

sections.h2: What to ask an Owatonna cash buyer
sections.html:
Get the offer in writing and read it line by line.

  • Which party orders the title work and pays for recording?
  • How will the buyer handle past flood or drainage issues in the disclosure?
  • If a rental license is active, who finishes the term?
  • What is the exact payout after deed tax and any county balance?

A direct offer lets you set the move date, and that is its main benefit over a listing. Weigh that against what an open-market sale would leave once repairs and months of upkeep are paid.

faqs.q: Does my Owatonna rental license transfer to a buyer?
faqs.a: A change of ownership calls for a new application, so the buyer applies for a license in their own name. The city issues two-year licenses once an inspection is passed and fees are paid.

faqs.q: How much is the state deed tax on a typical Owatonna sale?
faqs.a: The tax equals 0.33 percent of the price once the price passes $3,000, and a sale at or under that amount pays a flat $1.65. The county collects it at the recording stage.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Steele County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Go to the Finance office in the County Administration Building at 630 Florence Avenue, on the ground level, during weekday business hours. A drop box stands out front by the flagpoles.

faqs.q: What does a well disclosure cost in Steele County?
faqs.a: The recording office charges $54 for a well disclosure statement or certificate. The $46 deed recording fee is separate.

faqs.q: Should I mention the 2010 flood when selling an Owatonna house?
faqs.a: Yes, if your property is near the Straight River or Maple Creek and you know of water damage, mention it. The disclosure covers material facts you know of, and a buyer will look for flood history in that area.
